messages:
Lina: Heads-up  post-launch triage: we have a P1 in the auth flow (token refresh race) and ~5 small UX fixes that design wants in the next micro-sprint. Need a call on tradeoffs.
Omar: Auth issue is causing occasional 401 loops for a few customers after long idle sessions. Repro steps in the ticket.
Priya: UX fixes: button spacing on mobile, missing aria-labels, microcopy in onboarding, a tiny layout shift. Each is ~2-4h.
Nate: Auth root cause looks like concurrent refresh attempts hitting a shared cache invalidation. I can do a quick lock around refresh (est 1.5d) or a safer queuing refactor (est 1.5w).
QA-Ana: Acceptance for quick lock: no more 401 loops in our replayed sessions, plus unit test for concurrent refresh. We need a canary run 24h.
CS-Kevin: Affected customers escalated; they want either a fix or a temporary workaround. They'll accept a short maintenance window if we need it.
PM-Jordan: Options: A) Quick lock hotfix + ship small UI polishes now. B) Full refactor (better long-term) and delay polishes. My bias: rescue customers quickly then schedule refactor as an epic.
Lina: Also consider rolling back recent auth optimization flag. That would stop the issue immediately but roll back perf gains. Rollback is ~2h ops + validation.
Omar: Rollback path: flip flag -> monitor for regressions -> if ok, keep rollback until refactor done. Pro: fastest. Con: loses perf.
Priya: If we go hotfix, can we still squeeze the quick UI fixes into the same micro-sprint? Designers say they are important for onboarding conversions.
Nate: Team capacity: hotfix + 2 engineers on polishes is doable this sprint. Refactor must be planned as follow-on.
QA-Ana: Request: include the failing customer trace in regression tests, and add an e2e that simulates long idle sessions.
CS-Kevin: I'll prepare a short customer note offering a credit if they saw significant disruption. Keep language calm.
Lina: Proposal: Do not rollback flag yet. Ship emergency hotfix (lock) to unblock customers quickly, deploy to canary, run 24h. Parallel: ship the four UI polishes as quickwins. Schedule full refactor as "auth-refresh-refactor" epic in next planning with 8d estimate.
Omar: Agreed. I'll open branch `hotfix/auth-refresh-lock` and flag PR WIP. Link: https://github.com/redwood/auth/pull/999 (WIP).
SRE-Bot: Canary window requested: 2025-02-14T18:00Z for service "auth-gateway". Auto-rollback threshold: 0.2% error.
Nate: Hotfix PR ready in ~30h. QA window 12h. Can do polishes in parallel: PRs for UI fixes will be small branches: `ux/mobile-buttons`, `ux/aria-onboard`, etc.
QA-Ana: Running smoke once PR lands. Will add the idle-session e2e to CI.
Priya: Designers pushed minor copy adjustments to the branches. QA passed locally for spacing and copy.
CS-Kevin: I'll hold off on outbound comms until we see canary results, but customers notified they're in the loop.
Omar: Canary started. Observing logs now.
QA-Ana: Canary smoke looks good. No 401 loop repro for the traced sessions. Running 24h replay.
Lina: Backlog action: move the refactor to backlog -> epic "auth-refresh-refactor" and tag "follow-on:refactor". Move UI polish tickets to current sprint and mark owners.
Nate: If canary stays green, we'll promote to prod. If anything spikes, we flip rollback flag as emergency fallback.
SRE-Bot: Canary metrics 6h: 401-loop events dropped from 0.6% -> 0.02%. No perf regress beyond 3% p95.
PM-Jordan: Decision recap: emergency hotfix (lock) + ship UI polishes now. Refactor booked as follow-on epic with owner Omar. Customer comms: CS-Kevin to send update after prod.
Priya: Thanks all. Will update the design board and link PRs to tickets.
Omar: Merged hotfix to canary, starting production rollout in 2h if metrics hold.
SRE-Bot: Production rollout scheduled at 2025-02-15T09:00Z pending canary green. Monitoring channel: #prod-auth.
QA-Ana: Canary 24h complete: no 401 loops on traced sessions, e2e passed. Ready for prod.
CS-Kevin: Sending customer note: mitigation applied, refactor planned, refund offer if needed.
Lina: Closing thread: hotfix applied, polishes shipped, refactor on backlog. Thanks team :tada:
